MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
  December 17, 2012

1. OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:02 p.m. on Monday,
December 17, 2012, in the Council Chambers, Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

  b. Flag Salute

Councilmember Savidan led the salute to the flag.

  c. Invocation

Councilmember Traina gave the invocation.

  d. Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Savidan, Traina, Sanchez, and Mayor Estrada. Also present were City Manager Rock,
Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Community Services Director McPherron,
Public Works Director Damasse, Parks and Recreation Director Harding, Administrative
Services Director Chavez, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2. APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Savidan moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Gazeley seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

3.  SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

Recognition of the Narbonne High School Varsity Football Team for their outstanding season
and second straight Division 1 City Section Football Championship.

Mayor Estrada announced that this item will be moved to a future meeting in January 2013
since staff was unable to notify the team's coach regarding the City's planned recognition.

4.  CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock reminded everyone that the City of Lomita would be holding a community
meeting in Council Chambers at Lomita City Hall at 7 p.m. on Tuesday, December 18, 2012, in
order to provide information to the public regarding the blended water results and to conduct a
blind water taste testing.

5.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL
  Page 1 of 7
 Councilmember Traina requested that staff look into the possibility of obtaining grant funding for
the video surveillance of City streets.

Councilmember Sanchez reported that he attended a meeting of the League of California Cities.

Councilmember Gazeley reported that he attended the 3rd Annual Southern California
Association of Governments Economic Summit on December 10, 2012. Councilmember
Gazeley also stated that he attended Narbonne High School's State playoff football game.

6. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, announced that the owners of Tiffany’s Restaurant were unable
to renew their lease, and asked if the City’s economic development staff could possibly assist
the restaurant owners in their lease renewal efforts. Mr. McGrath also stated that there are
other competitive car sharing businesses similar to Car2Go, and if City Council approves
supporting Car2Go, then it could look as if preferential treatment is being given to one business.

Cindy Segawa, Lomita resident, stated that residents have the right to know about complaints
involving the Cypress Reservoir and the water in Lomita, and added that Councilmember’s
Traina request during the last City Council meeting was the right thing to request from staff.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, thanked Councilmember Gazeley and Charles Felix for
attending last Lomita Chamber of Commerce Business Mixer. Mr. Kivett stated that he is
familiar with the Car2Go car sharing concept, and supports the Car2Go program, which he
further stated might help residents with their transportation needs. Mr. Kivett also mentioned
that he strongly believes in transparency in government and the importance of residents
speaking on any matter in front of the City Council, as well as other Boards and Commissions.
Mr. Kivett went on to inform those in attendance that he was treated with disrespect during the
last Planning Commission, and he hoped that it would not happen again.

7. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Traina move to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Gazeley
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the City Council Meeting held on December
  3, 2012. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands

  d. Approval of an Agreement with Administrative Services CO-OP, d.b.a. South Bay Yellow
  Cab and United Checker Cab CO-OP, for Dial-A-Ride Services.  RECOMMEND
  APPROVAL.

  e. Approval of Resolution No. 2012-48 Adopting an Amended Conflict of Interest Code for the
  City of Lomita and Rescinding Resolution No. 2000-57. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
  Page 2 of 7
   f. Approval of Resolution No. 2012-49 Supporting in Concept the Car2Go Model.
  RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  g. Approval of Resolution No. 2012-50 Opposing Federal Sequestration (further cuts to
  federal programs that impact core local government programs).  RECOMMEND
  APPROVAL.

  PUBLIC HEARING

8.  INTERSECTION OF NARBONNE AVENUE AND 245TH STREET CROSSWALK

Community Services Director McPherron informed City Council that staff was evaluating the
possibility of removing the inoperable crosswalk at Narbonne Avenue and 245th Street.
According to Director McPherron, the Public Safety and Traffic Commission has already
reviewed this matter and recommended removal of the crosswalk.

Irena Guilmette, City of Lomita Traffic Advisor, presented a PowerPoint presentation
(Attachment A). Ms. Guilmette provided an overview of existing conditions, deficiencies
associated with the crosswalk, and traffic counts at the location. According to Ms. Guilmette, the
crosswalk is an uncontrolled school crosswalk with non-operating in-roadway warning lights that
are located at the southern approach of Narbonne Avenue and 245th Street. Furthermore, Ms.
Guilmette stated that the five-year collision history at the location, ending June 2012, indicated
only one pedestrian collision. Ms. Guilmette went on to recommended removal of the marked
crosswalk on Narbonne Avenue at 245th Street for the following reasons: it is preferable to have
pedestrians cross at the signalized intersection of Narbonne Avenue and Lomita Boulevard,
which is located 190 feet south of 245th Street; it is desirable to consolidate crossings in
downtown areas when crossing are too close to each other; there is currently minimal
pedestrian usage of the crosswalk at Narbonne Avenue and 245th Street; and that southbound
motorists on Narbonne Avenue block the crosswalk when traffic backups from the signal located
at Narbonne Avenue and Lomita Boulevard.

Director McPherron added that if the City Council approves the Public Safety and Traffic
Commission's recommendation to remove the crosswalk, notices will be posted at the crosswalk
for 30 days prior to scheduled removal in order to notify the public about upcoming removal of
the crosswalk. According to Director McPherron, the cost to remove crosswalk was estimated at
$16,330, with the funding for the cost to be allocated from the current and active Safe Routes to
Schools Grant.

Discussion followed as to the safety of pedestrians utilizing the crosswalk, from which direction
the majority of pedestrians come from, and whether school children were crossing at that
location.

Mayor Estrada opened the Public Hearing.

  Page 3 of 7
 Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, stated that he personally prefers using the crosswalk at
Narbonne Avenue and 245th Street, versus the intersection at Narbonne Avenue and Lomita
Boulevard. Mr. McGrath also mentioned that the intersection at Lomita and Narbonne was
optimized for motorists, not pedestrians, and is hard to cross.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, stated that the crosswalk in question was originally put in place
to create a walking downtown, and he suggested keeping the crosswalk and install blinking
lights in order to better ensure pedestrian safety.

Mayor Estrada closed the Public Hearing.

Councilmember Sanchez moved to approve the recommendation of the Public Safety and
Traffic Commission, and staff, for removal of the marked crosswalk, in-road warning lights, and
all accompanying crosswalk signs and equipment at Narbonne Avenue and 245th Street.
Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion.

Councilmember Savidan and Mayor Estrada commented that due to safety concerns, and
based on the Traffic Engineer's recommendation, it was reasonable to remove the crosswalk.

Councilmember Traina stated that the traffic collision at the crosswalk happened only because
the traffic lights were not operational at that time. Furthermore, Councilmember Traina
expressed his support of the walking downtown concept, and recommended keeping and
repairing the crosswalk at Narbonne Avenue and 245th Street, and possibly adding more lights in
order to make it more visible to oncoming motorists.

ROLL CALL:

AYES: Councilmembers Sanchez, Savidan, Gazeley, and Mayor Estrada.

NOES: Councilmember Traina.

  SCHEDULED MATTERS

9.  CYPRESS WATER PRODUCTION FACILITY (CWPF) OFFLINE TESTING FINAL
  REPORT
Public Works Director Damasse informed City Council that since the last City Council meeting
staff has initiated the public outreach campaign, and has conducted blind water taste testing at
several City meetings and events. According to Director Damasse, staff will be presenting water
taste testing results in early January 2013.

Members of the public took part in the blind water taste testing.

Lynn Grijalva, Consultant from Hazen and Sawyer, stated that since the last City Council
meeting, the data has not changed. Ms. Grijalva informed City Council that the results of the
well water testing have met all the goals established by the City Council prior to testing (i.e.,
hardness, total dissolved solids, and palatable taste). Furthermore, Ms. Grijalva announced that
based on the results of 110 people surveyed to date, about 29% of respondents could identify
the water correctly, while the other 71% could not differentiate between Metropolitan water and

  Page 4 of 7
 blended water. Ms. Grijalva added that the City of Lomita's well water meets all regulatory limits
based on the Title 22 results, except for manganese, which is removed to a “non-detectable”
level when well water is treated at the Cypress Water Production Facility (CWPF). Ms. Grijalva
also stated that no mercury was found in the water.

Ms. Grijalva mentioned that the City needs to continue their public outreach program and
continue to monitor the water system for corrosion, chlorine residuals, and scaling. Ms. Grijalva
also stated that since water changes all the time, it is important to optimize the CWPF and flush
the system periodically so that the water stays fresh. Furthermore, Ms. Grijalva also
recommended that old water pipelines be replaced. Finally, Ms. Grijalva concluded that based
on her evaluation, CWPF was ready to come back online.

In response to Councilmember Traina’s questions regarding scaling, Ms. Grijalva stated that
both blended and well water are within the range for scaling, with well water being at .5, and
blended water being between .3 to .4.

Councilmember Traina asked whether more testing is needed beyond the Title 22 testing. Ms.
Grijalva responded that Title 22 testing was comprehensive and designed to capture anything
that might occur with the water. Furthermore, Ms. Grijalva also pointed out that for the first three
years the City would be required to test their water every year, and then after the third year
water testing would be required once every three years.

Ms. Grijalva explained that water blending is done before the water gets to the tank, but once in
the tank, it is mixed there as well. Director Damasse further explained that it takes about a
week to get two different blends of 50/50 and 40/60 water; staff conducts one blending and then
drains the tank and blends again.

In response to questions of why water could have different tastes, Ms. Grijalva stated that it
could be due to chlorine concentration, water coming from different sources (Colorado River or
State project water), and/or from algae that can buildup when water stays in the reservoir for a
period of time during the summer.

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, requested that City Council consider getting reports about
complaints received by the City dealing with water. Mr. McGrath went on to state that City
Council needs to take responsibility and be more responsive to their constituents by being more
transparent. Mr. McGrath also asked City Council to review water rates, and possibly reduce
those rates if savings are found.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, expressed his concerns with calcium deposits in the pipes, the
hardness of the water, and the close proximity of CWPF to the landfill. Mr. Kivett also asked
City Council to consider testing the water every year.

Councilmember Sanchez stated that Water Subcommittee had a meeting on December 14th,
2012, where participants were able to ask more questions about the Reservoir, and discuss all
the things that need to be done to the tank. Councilmember Sanchez added that the goal is a
50/50 water blend, but staff will be monitoring the quality of the water and may vary the blend
based on quality concerns.

Councilmember Sanchez moved to accept the recommendation of staff and move forward with
  Page 5 of 7
 fixing the reservoir facility, and for staff to provide a report at a future meeting. Councilmember
Savidan seconded the motion.

Councilmember Traina mentioned that when the reservoir was online in 2010, a lot of
complaints were received by the City, and therefore it would be appropriate for City Council to
be periodically informed about future complaints regarding the Reservoir and quality of water.

Councilmember Gazeley thanked Councilmembers Sanchez and Savidan for their work on the
Water Subcommittee. Councilmember Gazeley also added that he was very pleased with the
quality of the blended water.

The motion carried unanimously.

2.  COMMENT LETTER ON THE PONTE VISTA DRAFT ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT
  REPORT (DEIR)

Assistant City Manager Sugano provided a PowerPoint presentation (Attachment B). Assistant
City Manager Sugano informed City Council that due to the location of the Ponte Vista project
being so close to the City of Lomita, the projected increase in traffic will significantly impact
Lomita. According to Assistant City Manager Sugano, as originally proposed, the Ponte Vista
project consisted of 2,300 residential units, 10,000 square feet of commercial space, and nine
acres of open space, but the revised project now proposes 1,135 residential units and
approximately five acres of open space. Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that staff's
concern with this project development is that its actual density is over 20 units per acre, which
will affect Lomita traffic counts and data; DEIR traffic counts and data are from 2010, which may
be outdated. The City has recommended two additional mitigation measures to ensure impacts
will be minimized: a pre-construction meeting with surrounding jurisdictions, and a two week
notification prior to the start of construction. Furthermore, the City of Lomita would prefer
Alternative C, which as outlined in the DEIR calls for only 830 residential units, instead of the
proposed 1,135 residential units. Assistant City Manager Sugano recommended that City
Council authorize the Mayor to sign the attached response letter to the City of Los Angeles.

Mayor Estrada suggested including R-1 in the letter, to which Council agreed. Councilmember
Savidan suggested including Pacific Coast Highway and Lomita Boulevard in the letter, as those
streets would also see influxes in traffic as well. Councilmember Traina asked that 262nd Street
be included as well.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, stated that he was familiar with the project DEIR, and added that
proposed density of the Ponte Vista project is less than in Lomita, and that the development of
the project would be a plus for Lomita by bringing people into the City to shop.

Councilmember Savidan moved to approve staff’s recommendation to sign the response letter
to the City of Los Angeles on the Ponte Vista Draft Environmental Impact Report, and include R-
1, as well as the other streets mentioned by Councilmembers (Pacific Coast Highway, Lomita
Boulevard, and 262nd Street). Councilmember Traina seconded the motion, which carried
unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

 Meeting adjourned at 8:40 p.m.

Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
